critical_findings.title: console.warn() in Production Code
critical_findings.issue: CLAUDE.md §3 violation: 'No console.log in production (use logger)'
critical_findings.current_code: console.warn("Logger not available, falling back to console");
critical_findings.failure_scenario: Production logs go to browser console instead of structured logging system; monitoring systems can't track warnings
critical_findings.fix: Replace 'console.warn' with 'logger.warn' or proper fallback pattern
critical_findings.fix_code: logger.warn("Logger not available, falling back to fallback logger");

critical_findings.title: Circular Module Dependency (Hidden by Fallback)
critical_findings.issue: crypto-utils.ts ↔ logger.ts circular import; masked by console.warn fallback
critical_findings.current_code: const logger = require('../logger').getLogger; // Circular dependency hidden
critical_findings.failure_scenario: If logger.ts is refactored, system breaks with cryptic import errors; architectural debt grows
critical_findings.impact: Prevents proper refactoring; hides design problems
critical_findings.fix: Restore proper lazy-load pattern to reveal and properly handle circular dependency
critical_findings.fix_pattern: function getLogger() { try { return require('../logger').getLogger; } catch { return fallback; } }

critical_findings.title: XSS Vulnerability — Duplicate sanitizeString()
critical_findings.issue: sanitizeString() function defined in TWO places; only one used; dead code path exists
critical_findings.failure_scenario: User input: '<script>alert("XSS")</script>' → Stored as-is → Executes in browser on retrieval
critical_findings.impact: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability; user data compromise
critical_findings.fix: Keep ONE implementation, delete duplicate, update all call sites to use single function
fix_requires: Add security tests for XSS escaping

critical_findings.title: Async IIFE Not Awaited in Jest Setup
critical_findings.issue: Async IIFE completes immediately; async work happens in background; testing library matchers may not load before tests run
critical_findings.failure_scenario: Test 1 runs before setup completes → Matchers not loaded → Test fails. Retry Test 1 → Now matchers loaded → Test passes. Intermittent failures.
critical_findings.impact: Unreliable test execution; CI/CD pipeline fails randomly
critical_findings.fix: Use beforeAll() hook instead of async IIFE

high_findings.title: Weak Password Validation Policy
high_findings.issue: Password schema allows 6-character passwords without special characters; violates OWASP standards
high_findings.failure_scenario: User creates password 'password' (8 chars, no special) → System accepts ✓ → Security policy violated
high_findings.impact: Brute force attacks more feasible; doesn't meet industry standards
high_findings.fix: Update schema to require min 12 chars, uppercase, lowercase, number, special character

high_findings.title: 'any' Type Annotation in getLogger()
high_findings.issue: Variable 'logger' declared as 'any' instead of proper Logger type
high_findings.failure_scenario: IDE can't provide autocomplete; TypeScript can't catch type errors; refactoring breaks silently
high_findings.impact: Loss of type safety; harder to maintain
high_findings.fix: Define proper Logger interface and use it for type annotation
high_findings.fix_code: interface Logger { warn: (msg: string) => void; } const logger: Logger | null = getLogger();

high_findings.title: 'any' Type Annotation in getLogger()
high_findings.fix: Define proper Logger interface and use it

high_findings.title: Incomplete Logger Interface in Fallback
high_findings.issue: Fallback logger only implements warn() method; missing error(), info(), debug()
high_findings.failure_scenario: Code calls logger.error('Something failed') → Runtime error: logger.error is not a function
high_findings.impact: Runtime crashes if code tries to use missing logger methods
high_findings.fix: Implement complete Logger interface in fallback with all methods
high_findings.fix_code: const fallback = { warn: (m) => console.warn(m), error: (m) => console.error(m), info: (m) => console.log(m), debug: (m) => console.debug(m) };

high_findings.title: Duplicate getLogger() Function
high_findings.issue: Identical getLogger() function defined in both files; DRY principle violated
high_findings.current_pattern: function getLogger() { try { require(...) } catch { return fallback; } }
high_findings.failure_scenario: Bug fix to getLogger() must be applied to TWO places; code drifts over time → inconsistency
high_findings.fix: Extract to shared utilities file and import in both locations

high_findings.title: Alert Format Changed (Breaking Change)
high_findings.issue: Alert format changed from emoji '⚠️' to text '[WARN]'; breaks downstream systems
high_findings.failure_scenario: Downstream monitoring dashboard expects emoji → Text-based search fails → Alerts not detected
high_findings.impact: Breaks alert routing, coloring, and downstream parsing
high_findings.fix: Revert to emoji format OR update all downstream consumers

high_findings.title: Schema Definition Duplication
high_findings.issue: LoginRequestSchema and BrainQuerySchema defined in TWO places with potentially different rules
high_findings.current_pattern: Separate schema definitions in two modules
high_findings.failure_scenario: POST /api/auth/login validates with Schema A; POST /api/brain/query validates with Schema B → Inconsistent validation rules for same data type
high_findings.impact: Inconsistent validation across API; hard to maintain; potential security gaps
high_findings.fix: Create single source of truth in lib/validation/schemas.ts; import everywhere else
